metadata.name: basename
metadata.displayName: basename - Strip directory and suffix from filenames
metadata.description: Strip directory and suffix from filenames

installation.note: basename is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: The basename command removes the directory path and optional suffix from a file path, returning just the filename. It's commonly used in scripts to extract filenames from full paths or to remove file extensions.
when_to_use: Extract filename from a full path
Remove file extension from a filename
Get just the filename without directory path
Remove common suffixes from multiple files

syntax.description: Remove leading directory components and optional trailing suffix from NAME. If SUFFIX is specified, it's removed from the end of the filename.

options.description: Support multiple arguments and treat each as a NAME
options.use_case: Process multiple file paths at once
Remove a specific suffix from multiple files

options.description: End each output line with NUL, not newline
options.use_case: Use with xargs -0 for handling filenames with spaces

misconceptions.title: basename modifies files
misconceptions.misconception: basename changes the actual file or removes the extension from the file
misconceptions.reality: basename only processes the string you provide - it doesn't modify files. It's purely a text manipulation command that works on path strings.
misconceptions.tip: basename is for string manipulation, not file operations. Use mv or rename to actually change filenames.

misconceptions.title: basename works on directories
misconceptions.misconception: basename only works on files, not directories
misconceptions.reality: basename works on any path string - files, directories, or even non-existent paths. It just processes the string.
misconceptions.tip: basename /path/to/directory returns 'directory' - it works on any path component.

common_pitfalls.description: The suffix must match the end of the filename exactly, including the dot
common_pitfalls.solution: Use '.txt' not 'txt'. The suffix is removed as-is, so 'file.txt' with suffix 'txt' won't work - use '.txt'

common_pitfalls.description: Paths with spaces will be split by the shell

related_commands.relationship: Complementary; dirname gets directory path, basename gets filename
related_commands.description: Strip last component from file name (gets directory)

related_commands.relationship: Text extraction; cut can extract path components, basename is specialized for filenames
related_commands.description: Remove sections from lines of files

best_practices: Always quote paths in scripts to handle spaces: basename "$filepath"
Use -s for consistent suffix removal across multiple files
Combine with dirname to split paths: dirname gets directory, basename gets filename
Use in scripts for clean filename extraction before processing
Remember basename doesn't modify files - it only processes strings
performance_tips: basename is very fast - negligible performance impact
Use -a for multiple files instead of calling basename multiple times
For very large batches, consider using find with -exec basename

additional_notes.path_manipulation: basename is part of a suite of path manipulation tools including dirname and realpath
additional_notes.scripting: Extremely common in shell scripts for filename processing
additional_notes.suffix_matching: Suffix matching is literal - must match exactly including the dot
additional_notes.complement: Often used with dirname: dirname gets the path, basename gets the filename
